summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Infertility is the inability of a couple to achieve clinical pregnancy after 2 years of regular unprotected coitus. IVF (In-Vitro Fertilization / Test-Tube Baby): ova and sperm are fertilized outside the body under sterile laboratory conditions. Post-fertilization Embryo Transfer (ET): (1) ZIFT (Zygote Intra-Fallopian Transfer): early embryo up to ≤8 blastomeres transferred into Fallopian Tube; (2) IUT (Intra-Uterine Transfer): embryo with >8 blastomeres transferred directly into Uterine cavity.

conceptBreakdown.content:
Infertility is medically defined as the inability of a couple to conceive or achieve clinical pregnancy despite **2 years** of regular, unprotected coitus.

### 9.1 The IVF-ET (In-Vitro Fertilization & Embryo Transfer) Protocol

```
                            IVF-ET PROTOCOL STAGES
                            
   Controlled Ovarian Hyper-stimulation (rFSH / hCG) ──► Transvaginal Ovum Retrieval
                                                                   │
   Sperm Processing & Capacitation in Culture Medium ──────────────┼─────────────────
                                                                   ▼
   In-Vitro Fertilization in Petri Dish ──► Zygote / Early Cleavage Formation
                                                                   │
   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   ▼                                                                                                                               ▼
   ZIFT (Zygote Intra-Fallopian Transfer)                                                                  IUT (Intra-Uterine Transfer)
   Embryo up to 8 BLASTOMERES transferred                                                                  Embryo > 8 BLASTOMERES (16–32 cells)
   into the FALLOPIAN TUBE.                                                                                transferred directly into UTERUS.
```

1. **ZIFT (Zygote Intra-Fallopian Transfer)**:
   - Zygote or early cleavage embryo containing **up to 8 blastomeres** is transferred into the ampullary-isthmic region of the Fallopian tube via laparoscopy.
   - Embryo completes natural transit, cleavage, and blastocyst formation in the oviduct before reaching the uterus for implantation.
2. **IUT (Intra-Uterine Transfer)**:
   - Advanced embryos containing **more than 8 blastomeres** (e.g., 16–32 celled morula or blastocyst) are transferred directly into the uterine cavity via a soft transcervical catheter.
3. **Surrogacy**: In cases where a female partner has severe uterine abnormalities, recurrent implantation failure, or absent uterus, the in-vitro fertilized embryo of the couple is transferred into the uterus of a surrogate mother.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Controlled Ovarian Hyperstimulation (COH)
conceptBreakdown.title: Controlled Ovarian Hyperstimulation (COH)
conceptBreakdown.content: GnRH agonists/antagonists downregulate endogenous pituitary gonadotropins, followed by recombinant FSH/hMG injections to stimulate multiple dominant follicles simultaneously (producing 8-15 oocytes).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Cryopreservation of Supernumerary Embryos
conceptBreakdown.title: Cryopreservation of Supernumerary Embryos
conceptBreakdown.content: Extra viable embryos from an IVF cycle are cryopreserved via vitrification in Liquid Nitrogen at -196°C for subsequent frozen embryo transfers (FET) without repeated ovarian stimulation.
